drivingQuestion: What exactly is removed with the crop, and how?
outcomeNote: Three tannaitic readings of benotzatah recorded without decision

segments.he: יָכוֹל יַקְדִּיר בְּסַכִּין וְיִטְּלֶנּוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בְּנֹצָתָהּ״ – נוֹטֵל אֶת הַנּוֹצָה עִמָּהּ. אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן חָנָן אוֹמֵר: נוֹטְלָהּ וְנוֹטֵל קוּרְקְבָנָהּ עִמָּהּ.
segments.en: Had the verse written only “its crop,” one «might» have thought that the priest may «cut» the skin «with a knife and take» the crop without any other part of the bird. Therefore, «the verse states: “With its feathers [benotzatah],”» which teaches that «he takes the feathers with it,» i.e., he must remove the skin with the feathers still attached. The Gemara presents another opinion: «Abba Yosei ben Ḥanan says: He takes» the crop «and he» also «takes its gizzard with it.»

segments.he: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל תָּנָא: ״בְּנֹצָתָהּ״ – בְּנוֹצָה שֶׁלָּהּ; קוֹדְרָהּ בְּסַכִּין כְּמִין אֲרוּבָּה.
segments.en: A Sage «from the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:» The word «benotzatah» is a contraction of the words «benotza shelah,» meaning its feathers. This teaches that the priest «cuts it with a knife,» creating an opening «like a window» opposite the crop. This allows him to remove the crop with only the feathers and skin directly opposite it, and that is what he brings to the place of the ashes.
